absent: Exact numeric values and bit positions for format flags, control commands, states, detach modes, and capabilities.
Field offsets and sizes for event, context, buffer, attribute, and file operation structures.
Semantics of context lock and unlock, removal from context, event read and count helpers, and primary identifier derivation.
Security check for event read, output redirection mechanics, filter handling, and attribute modification validation.
Scheduling, throttling, and physical unit start stop and period check behavior beyond the observed calls.
Ring buffer allocation, mapping, wakeup, and pause implementation details.
Packet filter program acquisition, attachment storage, and query mechanics.
Trace event flag definitions and offset computation for context bounds checking.
System wide sample rate limit value and inherit handling beyond pause warning.
Owner tracking and pending task work interaction with final reference release.

findings.text: Releases a performance event and all inherited children, detaching from its context and dropping references, always reporting success. Handles events never attached to a context as a special case requiring only reference release.
Returns aggregated counter value for an event plus its children together with enabled and running durations, acquiring the event context around the aggregation.
Disables an event under context protection and reports its current counter, optionally clearing the counter when reset is requested, with a warning if inheritance is configured.

Provides creation and release operations for mediated physical measurement units that are mutually exclusive with inclusive guest events, using atomic counters and returning busy when conflicting use exists.
Switches per CPU and task performance contexts for guest execution, scheduling out host state on load and scheduling it back on put, tracking loaded state per CPU.
Updates sampling frequency or period for an event under context protection after validation, delegating the actual application to a cross call executed in appropriate context.
File release hook for performance event descriptors that delegates to the kernel release routine and reports success.

File read hook that enforces a security check then dispatches to group or single value formatting under context protection, returning end of file for error state and no space when the caller buffer is smaller than required size.
Poll hook that waits on the event wait queue and reports hangup when no children remain, error for revoked or pinned error states, otherwise returns and clears the ring buffer poll flag.

Input output control dispatcher for enable, disable, reset, refresh, period, identifier query, output redirection, filter, packet filter attach and query, output pause, and attribute modification, rejecting revoked events and unknown commands.
An event without an attached context has never joined a context or group, so release only warns if attach state suggests otherwise and proceeds directly to reference release.
Group reads are only meaningful when parent and child agree on generation and sibling count; divergence is rejected to avoid summing inconsistent group configurations.
Co scheduled group members share enabled and running durations, so group reads publish a single pair from the leader combined with aggregated child totals rather than per member times.
Group read buffers begin with a member count equal to one plus sibling count, followed by per member count and optional identifier and lost sample fields according to requested format.
Single event reads return total count followed by optional enabled time, running time, identifier, and lost samples in a fixed order determined by format flags, with at most five values.

Inclusive guest events and mediated virtual machines cannot coexist; accounting fails with not supported or busy respectively when the opposite population is present, with fast paths when the own population is already nonzero.
When mediation support is compiled out, guest accounting operations unconditionally succeed or do nothing, so callers need no conditional logic.
Period updates require a sampling event and nonzero value, enforce a system wide frequency ceiling in frequency mode and physical unit validation plus high bit clearance in period mode.

Active events are stopped with update semantics, have pending period cleared, then restarted with reload semantics and unthrottled if the interrupt limit was reached, all bracketed by physical unit disable and enable.

Tracing events accept packet filter programs only for kernel probe, user probe, tracepoint, or system call tracepoint kinds, with strict program type correspondence and additional restrictions on sleepable, override, context write, and context offset.

Non tracing event handler attachment fails if a handler context already exists, if a program is already attached, if the program type mismatches, or if precise sampling with stack helper lacks full callchain configuration.
When packet filter support is unavailable, handler attachment reports not supported and tracing attachment reports missing entry, allowing callers to distinguish configuration from misuse.
Output redirection targets are recognized as performance descriptors by non empty file plus operation table identity, with negative one denoting empty output.
Reset refreshes hardware state via a read, zeroes the software counter, and refreshes the user visible page.
Group wide operations start from the group leader and visit every sibling and each of their inherited children, while child only operations visit the given event plus its direct children.

Release holds context protection while marking dead or detaching, then drops it before iteratively acquiring child mutex and target context mutex in nested order with reference pinning to avoid use after free.
Value aggregation and child list traversal require the child mutex, while the outer public wrappers additionally hold event context protection.

Group member traversal and counter sampling occur under the leader context interrupt saved spinlock, with child mutex of the leader held by the caller and parent context mutex conceptually pinning parent sibling structure.
Group reads and group wide iteration require the context mutex to stabilize group membership, asserted at entry.
Polling pins the ring buffer pointer with the mapping mutex to prevent concurrent output redirection from swapping the buffer and losing wakeups.
Guest context load and put require interrupts disabled and hold a combined per CPU and task context guard across disable, schedule, enable, and flag update.
First use transitions for guest events and mediated machines serialize on a dedicated mutex to check the opposite counter atomically before incrementing the own counter.
Output pause observes the ring buffer under read copy update protection and toggles paused state only when storage pages exist.

Performance event carries context pointer, lifecycle state, attach state, parent and group leader links, child and sibling lists with counts and generation, timing totals plus atomic child aggregates, counter and hardware period state, attributes, physical unit pointer, mapping mutex with ring buffer, wait queue, lost samples, read size, and filter and packet filter attachments.
Event context provides a mutex for membership stability, an interrupt safe spinlock for sampling, and an optional parent context pointer that must be null for directly operated events.
Ring buffer exposes page count, paused state, and a poll flag exchanged on poll; per CPU performance context tracks current task context and a per CPU guest loaded flag.
Release moves events beyond revoked through detached removal into dead, while already revoked or exited events transition directly to dead without detachment.
Events at or below revoked report error to pollers, events at or below exit with empty child list report hangup, and pinned error state additionally reports error.
Guest loaded flag is false in host mode, set true after scheduling out host and enabling guest contexts, and cleared after scheduling host back in, with warnings on redundant transitions.
Child removal drops and reacquires locks, so the first list entry must be revalidated before acting; otherwise a concurrently freed or replaced child could be mishandled.
Because group destruction is not atomic across differing contexts and parents may grow groups, readers must detect and abort on mismatched configurations instead of summing.
Group, single, identifier, period, filter, query, and attribute operations copy between user and kernel memory and must propagate fault failures without partial state change.
Control lookup acquires a program reference that must be released when attachment fails to avoid leaking.
Decrement paths warn if guest or machine counters are already zero, indicating unbalanced accounting or double release.
Read format uses PERF_FORMAT_GROUP to select group layout and optional PERF_FORMAT_TOTAL_TIME_ENABLED and PERF_FORMAT_TOTAL_TIME_RUNNING plus PERF_FORMAT_ID and PERF_FORMAT_LOST for extra fields.

Control interface defines PERF_EVENT_IOC_ENABLE and PERF_EVENT_IOC_DISABLE and PERF_EVENT_IOC_RESET and PERF_EVENT_IOC_REFRESH and PERF_EVENT_IOC_PERIOD and PERF_EVENT_IOC_ID and PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_OUTPUT and PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_FILTER and PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_BPF and PERF_EVENT_IOC_PAUSE_OUTPUT and PERF_EVENT_IOC_QUERY_BPF and PERF_EVENT_IOC_MODIFY_ATTRIBUTES plus PERF_IOC_FLAG_GROUP for group scope.

Operations signal ECHILD and ENODEV and ENOMEM and EFAULT and ENOSPC and EINVAL and EEXIST and EPROTO and EACCES and ENOENT and EOPNOTSUPP and EBUSY and ENOTTY and EBADF; poll signals EPOLLHUP and EPOLLERR.

Lifecycle distinguishes PERF_EVENT_STATE_ACTIVE and PERF_EVENT_STATE_ERROR and PERF_EVENT_STATE_EXIT and PERF_EVENT_STATE_REVOKED and PERF_EVENT_STATE_DEAD; detachment distinguishes DETACH_GROUP and DETACH_DEAD and DETACH_CHILD; guest switch uses EVENT_GUEST.

Guest inclusion depends on PERF_PMU_CAP_MEDIATED_VPMU with exclude guest attribute; sampling uses frequency versus period selection with MAX_INTERRUPTS throttle limit and PERF_EF_UPDATE with PERF_EF_RELOAD start stop semantics.
